text.p: Forest products company Weyerhaeuser Co. reported an increase in third-quarter profits Tuesday, citing strong lumber prices and improving pulp prices.
The world's largest private owner of marketable softwood timber posted net earnings of $119.7 million, or 60 cents a share, compared with $94.8 million, or 47 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.
However, third-quarter results in 1995 were depressed by a charge of $184.5 million, or 90 cents a share, mainly due to accounting changes.
The Federal Way, Wash.-based company recorded net sales of $2.85 billion vs. $3.04 billion a year ago.
Weyerhaeuser stock fell 50 cents to $45.625 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Our 1996 third-quarter results reflected strong lumber prices in both domestic and Japanese markets, and improving pulp prices," said Chief Executive Officer John Creighton Jr.
"The higher volumes and lower operating costs achieved by our business improvement plans help offset continuing weak pricing in paper and packaging products."
Operating earnings from Weyerhaeuser's timberlands and wood products rose to $210 million from $195.8 million a year ago.
But operating earnings from its pulp, paper and packaging products tumbled to $78.8 million, compared with $364.5 million in the third quarter of 1995.
Its real estate and financial services generated $5.2 million in operating earnings, a turnaround from $2.9 million in losses a year ago.
